summary: Sudden p95/p99 latency cliff after long-idle -> burst transitions in continuous batching
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring short windows (30s-3m) of elevated p95/p99 token latency and intermittent 504s immediately after long idle periods followed by traffic bursts. Behavior started after customer's migration to Dedicated pool with autoscaling enabled; reproducible in their prod us-east cluster.

Impact:
- Several API calls timed out (504) for a subset of requests during burst.
- Observed p95 rising from ~120ms to 800-1500ms and p99 up to 3s for 20-60s windows.
- Affects latency-sensitive features (live doc previews) for NimbleDocs; customer reports user-facing UI flicker and failed saves.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in prod-us-east
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.18-release
- Continuous-batcher service image: cbatcher-1.7.0
- Autoscaler: proprietary-pool-autoscaler v2.1
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Ensure a dedicated pool with zero recent traffic for >5 minutes.
2) Send a burst of ~200 small generation requests across 5 concurrent connections (prompt length ~20 tokens) at time T0.
3) Observe p95/p99 over next 2 minutes in Console per-route latency.
4) Repeat with different idle durations (1m, 5m, 15m) and note correlation with severity of spike.
logs:
Extracted excerpts (prod-us-east) 2026-03-01T14:02:11Z - 2026-03-01T14:05:00Z:
- continuous-batcher: INFO span=cbatch/window:start idle_window=312s chosen_window_ms=50
- continuous-batcher: WARN span=cbatch/dispatch delay_ms=810 queue_depth=37
- serving-runtime: WARN span=runtime/kvcache miss_rate=0.72 cold_kv_initialization=true
- api-gateway: ERROR 504 upstream_timeout route=/v1/generate status=504 trace_id=...
- autoscaler: INFO pool_scale=0 -> 2 reason=burst_detected scale_latency_s=28
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 15:00 - Support triage: Verified customer p95/p99 spikes aligned to bursts after idles; reproduced in repro cluster with same runtime and cbatcher image.
2026-03-01 16:30 - SRE observed that continuous-batcher chooses larger batch window after long idle: chosen_window_ms grows from typical 20-50ms up to 250-500ms in initial burst phase.

2026-03-01 18:00 - Hypothesis: cbatcher warmup logic waits for target batch occupancy or timer; after long idle the initial warmup loop creates head-of-line waiting as autoscaler also scales new GPUs, amplifying latency.
2026-03-02 09:10 - Tested a patch toggling aggressive idle backoff (PR linked). Initial patch reduced p95 by ~60% in isolated test but introduced slightly increased token fragmentation (tradeoff).
2026-03-02 11:45 - Observed KV cache cold-start contributing to per-request overhead; requests routed to freshly started workers had additional 150-300ms overhead while KV tables populated.
2026-03-02 14:20 - Correlation found between autoscaler scale latency (>20s) and severity of p99 spikes; when pool was warm (no scale up) spikes diminished.
2026-03-03 09:00 - Decided to implement a combination of faster initial batch timer, early-pass fast-path for tiny workloads, and proactive worker warmup hooks tied to autoscaler events.
comments: 2026-03-01 15:10  Aisha Patel (Support): Logged customer's raw request traces and shared initial reproducible steps. Noted UX impact; customer requests mitigation ASAP.

2026-03-01 16:40  Marco Chen (SRE): Reproduced locally. Continuous-batcher metrics show 'chosen_window_ms' spikes. Filing engineering investigation; tagging runtime team and autoscaler owners. Slack: #support, #sre-high.

2026-03-02 10:05  Elena Ruiz (Runtime Eng): Ran microbenchmarks. Found cold KV initialization and batch timer hysteresis both contributing. Opened PR to add early-pass batching timer and reduce idle backoff (see PR).
2026-03-02 12:30  NimbleDocs (Customer): Provided traces and consent to test fixes in their dedicated staging pool. Customer asked for temporary mitigations while fix rolls out.

2026-03-03 09:15  Marco Chen (SRE): Deployed canary of patched cbatcher to limited nodes in prod-us-east; initial telemetry shows p95 improvement during bursts, p99 tail largely reduced. Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-03 12:00  Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer of canary rollout and requested extended smoke test window.
resolution:
Partial mitigation deployed (2026-03-03):
- Canary release of cbatcher patch that shortens initial batching timer after idle and enables a tiny-workload fast-path.
- Added autoscaler->worker warmup hook to prepopulate KV caches when new nodes start scaling for a detected burst.
- Added Circuit alerting in Console: 'cbatcher.initial-window-ms > 200 && p99 > 1500ms' for prod-us-east.

Follow-ups:
- Roll out patch to full us-east pool if canary remains stable (follow-up task: INT-4311).
- Create customer-facing runbook entry explaining mitigation and recommended client backoff patterns (confluence page updated).
- Investigate long-term: adaptive warmup strategy that coordinates autoscaler and cbatcher (RFC in repo).
